data.title: IoT Hackathon
data.details:
IoT Hackathon:

A dynamic and inspiring event designed for tech enthusiasts, developers, and engineers to collaborate and innovate. Participants will engage in hands-on coding and problem-solving, leveraging connected devices to tackle real-world challenges. With a focus on redefining the boundaries of IoT applications, this hackathon serves as a platform for groundbreaking ideas and impactful solutions.

Problem Statements:

(Themes but not limited to):

Healthcare:

  • IoT-driven GPS Ambulance tracking for traffic-free transit
  • IoT-based Elderly Care Monitoring System
  • Real-time Guidance Assistant for Physically Disabled and Blind Individuals

Automation:

  • Smart Home Advancement for Automated Living
  • IoT-based Automatic Movable Dustbins
  • Fire Extinguishing Robot

Sustainability:

  • IoT-integrated intelligent energy management system for a sustainable future
  • IoT-enabled water management system for smarter homes
  • Industrial harmful gas detection and safety

Environmental:

  • IoT-Driven Precision Agriculture with farming solutions
  • Marine Litter Detection and Removal
  • Smart Wildlife Surveillance for Anti-Poaching

Guidelines:

  • The team leader is responsible for registering the team. Registration after the deadline will not be accepted.
  • Team members cannot be changed after registration.
  • The hackathon lasts 24 hours with 3 reviews. At least two team members must be available at the provided workspace at all times.
  • If participating in other events (e.g., workshops), teams must ensure proper time management.
  • Participants should be prepared to present their project at any time during the event, clearly representing each member’s contribution.
  • The team must submit all documents (code, PPT, flowchart, output image, etc.) to the GitHub repository (provided during the event) before attending the final review.
  • The judges' decision is final and must be followed.
  • Plagiarism will be strictly monitored—teams found using pre-existing projects from the internet or purchasing completed projects will be disqualified.
  • Refreshments will be provided; however, accommodation and food will NOT be provided.
  • Participants must bring their own laptops and required components for the event.
  • The organizing team will provide components based on availability and the time required for purchasing.
  • Teams must provide a list of required components during registration.
  • The organizing team will confirm component availability 7-10 days before the event, and teams should plan alternatives accordingly.

data.title: Capture the Flag
data.details:
Unleash your inner cyber detective and embark on a journey through the fascinating realms of ethical hacking, digital forensics, cryptography, and system exploitation. Whether you're a seasoned hacker sharpening your expertise or a curious beginner exploring the thrilling universe of cybersecurity, this CTF promises to test your problem-solving abilities and strategic thinking like never before. Get ready to tackle adrenaline-pumping challenges, decode mysteries, and conquer the digital battlefield in an electrifying competitive environment.

Guidelines: 

  • General Rules:
    • Participants must register as a team (Team size. 2-3 members).
    • The event will run for a specified duration. All challenges must be completed within this timeframe.
    • Any attempt to disrupt the CTF platform or other participants will result in immediate disqualification unless explicitly mentioned.
    • The use of automated tools for solving challenges is prohibited unless explicitly allowed.
    • The use of AI and AI-powered tools to solve challenges is strictly prohibited unless explicitly allowed for specific tasks.
    • No physical machines or devices will be provided for attack purposes.
    • Sharing or discussing flags with other teams is strictly forbidden.
  • Code of Conduct:
    • Follow the event's communication guidelines, including using only designated channels for queries or discussions.
  • Challenge Rules:
    • Challenges may include categories such as web exploitation, cryptography, reverse engineering, forensics, and binary exploitation.
    • Each challenge will have a specific point value based on its difficulty.
    • Teams must submit flags in the correct format to earn points (e.g., CTF{example_flag}).
    • If you believe a challenge is broken or unclear, notify the organizers through the official communication channel. Do not exploit errors in challenge deployment.
  • Platform Use:
    • Only one account per team is allowed on the CTF platform.
    • Teams are responsible for the security of their account credentials.
    • Do not attack the CTF platform itself, including attempting to access unauthorized areas or data.
  • Disqualification Criteria:
    • Engaging in prohibited activities, including:
      • Sharing flags or collaborating with other teams.
      • Attacking other participants or the CTF infrastructure.
      • Using unauthorized tools or scripts.
    • Violating any rule will lead to immediate disqualification and removal from the event.
    • The decision of the event organizers is final and binding in all matters.
  • Termination Clause
    • The organizers reserve the right to modify or terminate the event if unforeseen circumstances arise.

data.title: Cyber-O-Day 2.0
data.details:
Registration Link: https://vtopcc6.vit.ac.in/chennai-events/eventPreview/326

Cyber-O-Day 2.0 is a 24-Hour event organized by Linux Club scheduled for October 6th and 7th, 2023, dedicated to imparting crucial knowledge about today's most pressing societal concerns: Cybersecurity and Ethical Hacking. It’s a structured and entirely hands-on workshop run by our own technical team. The topics that will be covered are:

Linux Fundamentals: Linux Fundamentals are the building blocks of understanding the Linux operating system, which is pivotal in cybersecurity. Participants will delve into the core concepts, file structure, and command-line interface, gaining essential skills for server management and security analysis.

Cryptography: Cryptography forms the bedrock of secure communication and data protection. This segment explores encryption, decryption, and cryptographic protocols that safeguard information integrity, confidentiality, and authentication in the digital realm.

OSINT and Reconnaissance: Open-source Intelligence (OSINT) and Reconnaissance involve honing skills to gather critical information about potential targets. Participants will learn techniques for sourcing data from publicly available resources, a key component in cybersecurity threat assessment.

Web Exploitation: Web Exploitation skills are vital for identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities in web applications, potentially leading to unauthorized access or data breaches. Participants will discover methods for recognizing and mitigating these risks, a critical skill in defending against cyberattacks.

Binary Exploitation: Binary Exploitation is crucial for delving into the low-level intricacies of software, enabling the analysis of vulnerabilities and protection against malicious attacks. Participants will learn the art of securing software at its core, strengthening their cybersecurity toolkit.

What will you win?

  • INR 10K+ cash prizes
  • Participation certificates for all

data.title: PASSWORD
data.details:
Events Detail:

The first day of the event will be a workshop taken up by the Technical department of the club, the workshop will ensure that the participants will learn about all the topics in detail with a hands-on experience and how to use them in real time applications.

The workshop is handled by:

  • Abhishek (President), who is well versed in cyber security, windows, and Android hacking
  • Aditya (Vice President), has the best knowledge about networking and CTF
  • Animesh (Technical head), has hands-on experience in hardware, Operating Systems and cybersecurity

The workshop mainly focuses on-

Introduction to Cybersecurity: 

  • Importance of cybersecurity in the digital age
  • Overview of common security threats and attack vectors

Steganography:

  • Understanding steganography and its applications
  • Techniques for hiding information within digital media
  • Practical examples and demonstrations of steganography tools

Web Exploitation: 

  • Introduction to web vulnerabilities (e.g., SQL injection, cross-site scripting)
  • Hands-on exercises on identifying and exploiting web vulnerabilities
  • Best practices for secure web development and defense against attacks

Reverse Engineering:

  • Basics of reverse engineering and its significance in cybersecurity
  • Introduction to disassemblers and debuggers
  • Practical exercises on analyzing and reverse engineering simple programs

Basic Linux:

  • Introduction to the Linux operating system
  • Command line basics and essential Linux commands
  • Hands-on exercises on navigating and managing files and directories in Linux

Binary Exploitation:

  • Introduction to binary exploitation techniques
  • Understanding buffer overflows and memory corruption vulnerabilities
  • Practical exercises on exploiting binary programs

The main event takes place on the second day of the event, the event is titled "Password." This unique event aims to provide participants with an all-inclusive event that covers a wide range of skills and challenges. The name "Password" signifies the depth and theme of the event, symbolizing our commitment to offering a comprehensive platform for participants to explore and showcase their expertise.

The event consists of three sessions, each offering a unique and engaging experience. The first session features a captivating Capture the Flag (CTF) competition with 25 challenges covering topics like basic Linux and binary exploitation created by our team. Participants will test their knowledge and skills in a continuous competition format, with hidden hints embedded in a customized operating system specially customized for this event. In the second session, we have remote machine round, an exciting Escape the Room challenge. Participants will be given a remote machine and tasked with acquiring a key

In third round once they obtain key in the second round , they have to enter the key into a safe, unlocking it and earning themselves a well-deserved trophy.

data.title: GPU Hackathon 2023
data.details:
Together with NVIDIA and OpenACC.org, Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) will host a virtual Hackathon starting August 15 and concluding August 24, 2023. Open Hackathons provide exciting opportunities for scientists to accelerate their AI or HPC research under the guidance of expert mentors from national laboratories, universities and industry leaders in a collaborative environment. Representing distinguished scholars and preeminent institutions around the world, these teams of mentors and attendees work together to realize performance gains and speedups using a variety of programming models, libraries and tools.

Goal:

The goal of the Open Hackathon is for computational scientists to port, accelerate and optimize their scientific applications to modern computer architectures, including CPUs, GPUs and other computing technologies. Participating teams should leave the event either with their applications accelerated and/or optimized on the latest supercomputing hardware or a clear roadmap of the next steps needed to leverage these resources.

Prerequisites:

This Hackathon is open to everyone looking to take their projects to the next level; however, priority acceptance will be given to BNL-affiliated scientists and their collaborators.

  • Teams are expected to be fluent with the code or project they bring to the event and motivated to make progress during the hackathon.
  • A minimum of 3 team members must participate throughout the entire event.
  • Lack of participation for the duration of the Hackathon may cause the entire team to be excused.
    Projects brought to the event are required to have a license attached and detailed in the application.

data.title: Cyberheist - Capture the Flag (CTF)
data.details:
Are you ready to take your cybersecurity skills to the next level? Join our upcoming CTF (Capture the Flag) event and compete for cash prizes worth INR 6000 and an exclusive internship opportunity!

CYBERHEIST CTF event is a thrilling competition designed for individuals and teams of all skill levels. You will be presented with a variety of security-related challenges, such as decoding encrypted messages, finding vulnerabilities in web applications, and reverse engineering binary files. As you successfully solve each challenge, you will be rewarded with a "flag" that you must submit to the organizers to prove completion.

But the competition isn't just about winning, it's also about learning and improving. Our CTF event is a great opportunity to learn new techniques, tools, and strategies, as well as to network with other security enthusiasts.

And the rewards are worth the effort, the top-performing teams or individuals will be awarded with cash prizes worth INR 6000 and an exclusive internship opportunity where you will have the chance to work with industry experts and gain valuable hands-on experience.

Don't miss out on this exciting opportunity to test your skills, win prizes and advance your career.

  • Offline Mode
  • Three Rounds
  • Date - 27-28 January 2023
  • Duration 3 hours
  • Timing 12:00 pm to 3:00 pm
  • Team Size 1-4
  • Platform :- Ctfd

Instructions

  • There will be a set of challenges from a range of categories like cryptography, web security, forensics, steganography, reverse engineering, binary exploits, etc.
  • The challenges can either be a collection of files that they can download and find the “Flag” or can be running as web services to which the participants connect and exploit to retrieve the Flag.

data.title: Google Code Jam
data.details:
Pump up the Code Jam!

Google’s longest-running global coding competition, Code Jam, call on programmers around the world to solve challenging, algorithmic puzzles against the clock. Contestants advance through four online-hosted rounds to compete at the annual Code Jam World Finals that is held at a different international Google office each year. Each round brings new challenges, and in the end, 25 contestants will have the ultimate chance to put their skills to the test, vying for cash prizes and the coveted championship title at the World Finals.

Register and compete in Code Jam’s Online Qualification Round. It lasts 27 hours, but you won't need that long to earn the round’s qualifying point minimum. Once you do, you’ll advance to Online Round 1. We offer three sub-rounds for Round 1, and you can compete in as many as it takes for you to finish in the top 1,500 of any of these rounds.

The top 1,500 from each sub-round move on to compete for a spot in the top 1,000 contestants of Code Jam Online Round 2. These top 1,000 contestants advance to Online Round 3 and earn a limited edition Code Jam t-shirt.

The top 25 contestants from Code Jam Online Round 3 will compete in the Virtual World Finals for the championship title and a cash prize of $15,000 USD.

Eligibility:

The exact details are explained in the Terms, but here are some of the requirements that you have to meet at the time of registration:

  • You are 16 years of age or older. Only those who are 18 years of age or older around the time of the final round (see theTerms for the exact date) are eligible to attend the onsite finals.
  • You are not a current employee/intern of Google Inc. or an employee of any Google affiliate or subsidiary. If you have a job offer from Google, you must stop competing when you become an employee. Note that if you advance to the final round, and become a Google employee before the final round, you will not be eligible to travel to or compete in the final round.
  • You are not an immediate family member (parent, child, sibling, or spouse) of, or living in the same household as, a Google employee or an employee of any Google affiliate or subsidiary.
  • You are not a resident of Quebec, Crimea, North Korea, or anywhere that the contest is prohibited by law.
  • You will be disqualified if you gained information on a problem as a participant in a Google-managed program or by working as an employee, intern, contractor, director, officer, or other official office-holder of Google, you will be disqualified from a contest if you submit a submission for that problem.

Description: An Auction + Coding Competition

Programming problems will be auctioned off, which then needs to be solved. Auctioneers and Coders will not be able to interact with each other. Coders will take turns solving the questions bought by their respective auctioneers. The fastest correct solvers would emerge victorious.

Rules and regulations:

  • Open to all
  • Only students who registered before the deadline will be eligible for the competition.
  • The decisions made by the event in charges regarding discrepancies will be final and binding.
  • Team Size - Min - 3 (1 for auction, 2 coders) , Max- 4(2 for auction, 2 coders)
  • Cross-college teams are also allowed.

Prelims (Offline):

  • Questions will be asked from topics regarding basic coding knowledge, data structure and one of the three language choices-Python/C++/Java 
  • Answers will be collected through Quiziz and Top (10-12 teams) scorers will qualify for the next round. Ties will be based on the Time of Submission.

Finals (Offline):

  • The events will be conducted simultaneously in 2 rooms, one where a live auction is being conducted and the other where coding will begin.
  • The virtual currency will be provided to each team, with the top 3 teams of the prelims getting a bit advantage (extra amount).
  • The moment a team purchases a question, it will be given to respective teammates in the coding room, for time advantage for early purchasing.
  • After the last question is sold, there will be an extra one hour for all teams to finish their codes
  • Total Score will be calculated based on - 
    • Total Questions Solved of varying difficulty level (Easy /Medium/ Hard)
    • The remaining Points (currency) after the end of the auction will be added to the score
  • Ties will be resolved on time of completion of all the codes.(OR the last successful submission done Earliest)

data.title: Codelocks
data.details:
The Lockout tournament would span over about 3 hours. It will be a 1v1 knockout tournament i.e. if someone loses a single match, they will be out of the tournament. In the first round, 32 matches will be played (taking a strength of 64) and 32 participants will proceed to the next round. After 5 rounds, we will get the winner of the tournament. It will be an offline event in which the participants would be required to bring their laptops and join a discord server to participate in the tournament. 

Guidelines:

  • Only lone wolves are welcome.
  • The tournament is open to all college students.
  • Every participant must carry an ID card.
  • Scores will be displayed after every round.
  • Use of any unfair means will lead to disqualification.

Rules:

  • Matches will be run on Discord Lockout Bot.
  • Contest time will be 20 minutes (30 minutes for Semi-Finals and Finals)
  • The contest will have five questions with increasing difficulty and score.
  • If a player solves a question first, then their opponent CANNOT attempt that question.
  • The player with a higher score at the end, or the player to reach a score greater than or equal to 800, wins the Lockout.
  • In case of a tie the player who has done the higher weightage problem wins.

data.title: Password 2024
data.details:
All that you need to know about PASSWORD '24:

|Please follow the procedures on the site to create your account and then proceed to register and pay.

The Prevent CTF is currently active. Engage in the challenge to accumulate coins, which can later be utilized in the Password Event to access hints without impacting your overall score.

Team Size: 1-3

Pre-Event Period:

  • The online event will begin 1 week before the actual physical event.
  • Challenges (not just CTFs) will be provided during this period.
  • Participants can collect coins during the week.
  • Coins can be utilized on the event day.
  • Challenges will be easy to lower level to maintain motivation.

Event Overview:

Divided into two main segments, a Jeopardy Style CTF and an Attack-Defense Style CTF, participants will face challenges, learn, and compete for exciting prizes.

Jeopardy Style CTF:

In this session, participants will face a grid of challenges resembling the popular Jeopardy game format. All questions will be visible simultaneously, offering a comprehensive view of the playing field. The dynamic points system adds an extra layer of excitement—each challenge starts with 500 points, and as more participants conquer a challenge, its points decrease for everyone.

Attack-Defense Style CTF:

Dive into the heart of cybersecurity warfare with our Attack-Defense style CTF. Teams will be divided into 10 factions, each comprising approximately 20 teams. Each faction will have access to a dedicated server loaded with various vulnerabilities, providing a real-world simulation for participants.

Faction Allocation for Attack-Defense Style CTF:

Teams will be divided into factions cyclically based on their Round 1 (Jeopardy Style CTF) score. 

Winner Selection:

  • Final points = Jeopardy Style CTF (Round 1) + Attack-Defense Style CTF (Round 2)
  • 1st, 2nd, and 3rd based on the final score.

Prizes and Goodies:

  • 1st Position: Rs. 5000
  • 2nd Position: Rs. 3000
  • 3rd Position: Rs. 2000

Goodies for all teams of the winning faction.

data.details:
Welcome to the ultimate AI hackathon extravaganza!

Are you ready to put your technical skills to the test and compete against the brightest minds in the game? This is your chance to show off your creative prowess, and build something amazing. We can guarantee that this is not your average hackathon.

  • Eligibility: The hackathon is open to individuals or teams of up to four members. Participants must be at least 18 years of age and have access to the internet.
  • Registration: Participants must register for the hackathon using the Unstop platform. Registrations will be accepted up until the day of the hackathon.
  • Submission Guidelines: All submissions must be made on the Unstop platform. Participants must submit their project source code, a presentation of their project, and a short video demo of their project.

    • User experience and interface design

  • Judging Process: The judging process will be done by a panel of judges with expertise in AI. The panel will evaluate and score all submissions based on the criteria mentioned above.
  • Prizes: The top three projects will be awarded prizes. The prizes will be announced before the hackathon starts.
  • Code of Conduct: Participants must abide by a code of conduct that ensures respect for all participants, judges, and organizers. Any form of harassment or discrimination will not be tolerated and may lead to disqualification.
  • Intellectual Property: All submissions will remain the property of the participants. However, the organizers reserve the right to use submitted materials for promotional purposes.
  • Disqualification: The organizers reserve the right to disqualify any submission that violates any of the rules and regulations.

data.title: Code Hunt
data.details:
Use "EARLY BIRD" coupon for Early Bird. Offer valid till 16th march.

The coding club’s treasure has been stolen by a mysterious being Deadbug. Deadbug shall give the treasure only to the chosen ones. The treasure shall only be revealed when a ritual called Code Hunt is performed.

CodeHunt is a team contest where teams have to solve a problem to get a hint about a location. At the site, team members are required to solve a puzzle to get the next question.

The team which has the maximum points with least time shall win.

Rules:

  • It is an offline team based event.the team will be divided into 2 halves, one will be the coding half and other will be the hunters (physical team who will solve the aptitude problems).
  • There will be a team of 2-4 members and at least one of them should be a coder.
  • Each team have to bring their own laptop.
  • Duration of the event will be two and a half hour.
  • Each team will be given a problem and their task is to write a program that solves each problem as a coding part and then the hunters will solve the aptitude questions. and the cycle will continue.
  • Judging Criteria will be as per icpc style where time penalty includes both time taken to solve coding question as well as aptitude question. There will be 10 minutes penalty for each incorrect answer (Coding or aptitude).
  • More information will be provided at the time of contest itself.
  • if any team member is found committing any malpractice, the whole team will be disqualified from all the upcoming coding events.
  • The decision of the organizers shall be treated as final and binding.
